Manages care coordination for a designated panel of patients, emphasizing health promotion, chronic care management, patient self-management support, and overall wellness.

Demonstrates a collaborative team approach for managing patient panels, ensuring continuity and quality of care tailored to individual patient goals and needs.

Monitors assigned PACT metrics and uses VHA panel-management tools to identify care gaps, prepare patient data, and support proactive, high-quality primary care delivery.

Identifies and manages assigned patients requiring RN care through daily huddles and team collaboration; develops individualized care, provides health coaching and motivational interviewing, and delivers ongoing management for patients with chronic and ambulatory care-sensitive conditions.

Physical Requirements: Must be able to perform all duties without restriction including: Driving, significant standing, walking, stooping, bending, reaching, lifting, and turning.

Responsibilities include repositioning individuals and assisting with transfers to wheelchairs or stretchers. Mechanical lifting devices must be used when available for heavy or difficult transfers. The work may require lifting or pushing more than 50 pounds and using stairs regularly.

Adequate visual and auditory acuity is necessary to provide safe and effective care. The position may require working with arms above shoulder level, or with the neck fully flexed or extended for certain periods. It also requires the ability to maintain physical control or self-protection if encountering physically aggressive individuals.

There may be exposure to infectious patients or contaminated materials, requiring the use of protective clothing during isolation or invasive procedures. Occasionally, the role involves interacting with individuals who are combative due to conditions such as delirium, dementia, or psychiatric disorders.

The individual in this role must be mature, flexible, and capable of working effectively in stressful situations, adjusting priorities as needed.

Duties include but not limited to: The Nurse Outpatient Staff Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based outpatient care to patients with oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants as appropriate to the setting.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient transition through the continuum of patient care, patient and family education, patient self-management after discharge, and supporting factors that impact customer satisfaction.

The nurse will assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and enhance outcomes utilization. This nurse integrates outpatient knowledge, skills, abilities, and judgment and is self-directed in goal setting for managing complex situations.

Validates understanding of the rationale for care processes and decisions. Questions clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care. The nurse will demonstrate the ability to cope with and manage competing priorities.

The nurse demonstrates competence in outpatient practice and decision­ making, deliberate planning, and critical thinking skills. The incumbent is responsible to the assigned rating and approving supervisors and is accountable to the Associate Director of Patient Care Services (ADPCS). Also: 1.

Independently plans and delivers technically competent care to patients with complex needs in alignment with the ANA Standards of Nursing Practice. 2. Manages the care of patients, while organizing and prioritizing patient care needs, and ensuring assigned tasks are completed. 3.

Functions as an emerging leader in providing direction to staff to identify, implement and evaluate patient care needs. 4. Collaborates with the interdisciplinary team to ensure the plan of care is achieved.

The Community Care Nurse Manager practicing in the Supervisory path is a nurse who provides indirect or direct nursing care to patients and families. The Nurse Manager utilizes the nursing process to assist, plan, implement and evaluate Community Care.

The Nurse Manager provides supervision of clinical staff and has continuing responsibility for the following functions: 1. Planning work to be accomplished by subordinates, setting priorities, preparing schedules for completion of work, 2.

Assigning work to subordinates based on priorities considering the difficulty and the requirements of the assignments and the capabilities of subordinates, 3. Evaluating the performance of subordinates, 4. Making recommendations for appointments, advancements or reassignments of subordinates, 5.

Giving advice, counsel, or instruction to subordinate personnel on work and administrative matters, 6. Hearing and resolving complaints of subordinates and referring more serious complaints not resolved to a higher-level supervisor, 7. Recommending and/or taking disciplinary action where appropriate, 8.

Identifying developmental and training needs of subordinates and providing or making provision for such development and training (VA Handbook, 5007, Pan M Chapter 8) and other duties as assigned.

In addition, the Community Care Nurse Manger takes responsibility for role specific standards of care and practice, performance improvement, coaching staff, customer service and patient satisfaction, the work environment, patient and employee safety, and accreditation and regulatory standards.

He/she possesses intimate knowledge of Fee federal regulations, VHA guidelines, medical review criteria, utilization management processes, clinical documentation requirements, current standards of care, and compliance guidelines.

The incumbent supports the medical center's mission by possessing and exemplifying the core competencies of the High-Performance Model. The Community Care Nurse Manager actively develops and manages collaborative partnerships with physicians and providers both within and outside of VASDHS and other clinicians involved in health care delivery.

Blind Rehabilitation Center (BRC) Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible and accountable for individual nursing practice and determines the appropriate delegation of tasks consistent with the nurse's obligation to provide optimal care. The focus is on individual growth and development in practice with increased levels of self-direction.

Ability to formulate a plan of care based on nursing assessments. Seeks guidance in how to improve care provided to Veterans and families. The nurse brings principles and theory with limited application of critical thinking skills. The BRC RN is knowledgeable and adheres to Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities (CARF) standards.

Duties are as follows but not limited too: Applies clinical knowledge/judgment to lead staff involvement in planning, decision-making, and evaluating outcomes within the immediate practice setting. Effectively functions as a leader, with demonstrated outcomes, for the immediate practice setting.

Improves Veteran/patient driven care by resolving experience issues such as coordination of care, timeliness or process issues, common themes of dissatisfaction, or environment of care concerns for the immediate practice setting.

Applies patient, family, and caregiver knowledge, values, and beliefs into care delivery without judgement or discrimination. Serves as an advocate for patients, families, and caregivers, improving outcomes for the immediate practice setting.

Serves as a resource for patients, caregivers, and staff to address and resolve ethical issues in the immediate practice setting. Leads the implementation of high reliability principles and I CARE values to increase consistency of care delivered and improve patient outcomes.

Demonstrates the ability to improve the effectiveness of communication and interactions with others, to inspire their cooperation and confidence to ensure safe and effective outcomes in the current practice setting. Leads teams, contributes to team conferences, and actively collaborates in all phases of patient care planning.

Successfully integrates objectives, opportunities, and resources. Expands knowledge base and practice evaluation through mentoring, precepting, and/or teaching to improve outcomes in the immediate practice setting. Leads education initiatives to expand knowledge with improved outcomes in the immediate practice setting.

Takes responsibility for personal and professional career goals. Supports the professional growth of others. Participates in the advancement of the profession through mentoring, precepting, and/or teaching. Participates in the development, implementation, and evaluation of interdisciplinary care.

Establishes a therapeutic relationship, allowing the patient to attain, maintain or regain optimal function through assessment and treatment. Knowledgeable of ethical issues related to professional nursing practice and follows established policies of the practice setting, VA, and ANA Code of Ethics for Nurses.

Aware of high reliability principles to deliver consistent care and improve patient outcomes. Demonstrates positive, effective communication skills and professional behaviors that promote cooperation and teamwork with internal and external customers. Participates in unit based educational activities and continuing education requirements.

Responsible for maintaining competency to continue personal and professional growth. Applies evidence-based practice/research to patient care. Participates in unit-based activities to improve and deliver cost effective patient care. Demonstrates knowledge of specific unit level performance improvement activities.

Incorporates patient preferences into shared care delivery decisions.

The Nurse Practitioner (NP) is a licensed independent practitioner with advanced education and national certification who provides evidence-based care for a population of patients.

The major duties and responsibilities of the position include: Independently manages a panel of patients with acute and chronic health conditions with an emphasis on health promotion and disease prevention using evidence-based practice. Develops and implements an individualized plan to achieve optimal population health and disease management.

Demonstrates leadership and works collaboratively with the interdisciplinary team. Orders and interprets labs, tests, and diagnostic studies. Prescribes pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic interventions. Initiates referrals and consults to specialty services. Provides education to patients and their families.

Assesses and adjusts the plan of care as needed to achieve optimal patient outcomes.

(Applicants pending the completion of educational requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until the education requirements are met.) Must be a graduate of a school of professional nursing approved by the appropriate accrediting agency and accredited by one of the following accrediting bodies at the time the program was completed by the applicant: The Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

NOTE: Foreign Education. Graduates of foreign schools of professional nursing programs, the nurse practitioner degree equivalency must be validated through an Agency recognized degree equivalency evaluation agency, such as the International Consultants of Delaware (ICD).

Candidates with equivalent nurse practitioner masters or doctorate level degrees who possess current, full, active, and unrestricted registration and certification will meet the requirement of graduation from an approved school of professional nursing to warrant appointment.

License - All APN (NPs) must possess and maintain an active, current, full, and unrestricted APN license to practice as an NP in a State, Territory or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Basic Board Certification - All APN (NPs) must maintain full and current basic board certification in one of the following: Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP), Adult Nurse Practitioner (ANP), Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner (AGPCNP), Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (ACNP), Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP), or Gerontology Nurse Practitioner (GNP) from one of the following: the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), American Academy of Nurse Practitioners Certification Board (AANPCB), or other nationally recognized certifying body in the area in which the Nurse Practitioner is academically prepared.

The Registered Nurse is responsible for: Enrolling and providing telehealth care for Veterans in all Nationally Designated Telehealth Hub (NDTH) programs. NDTH consists of Tele Palliative Care, Tele Post Intensive Care Recovery, Tele Recovery and Resilience Program and Tele Geriatrics.

The nurse will screen Veterans for enrollment to NDTH programs using criteria and screening tools. The nurse will assess using these screening tools and interview questions as to whether the Veteran requires monitoring by the program for their chronic symptoms, palliative care, post intensive care syndrome, and chronic illness.

The nurse will contact Veterans daily by video connect and/or phone to conduct interviews, assessments, and schedule appointments. The nurse will educate Veterans on how to use equipment that includes, but not limited to, pulse oximeter, incentive spirometer and if needed blood pressure machine.

The nurse is responsible for their cohort of Veterans providing case management, education, and regular nursing visits to provide care and help Veterans reach their goals. The nurse will work with an Interdisciplinary Team.

The nurse must assess and understand when to report an assessment to the physician, psychologist, pharmacist, social worker, and other disciplines as appropriate. The nurse will help to train new staff and re-educate current staff as needed. The nurse will participate in IDT and family meetings and communicate information about their patients.

The nurse will be responsible for the submitting individualized slides for presentation during the IDT meeting. The program is constantly evolving, and your duties may increase or decrease over time. The nurse is expected to be flexible when needed to provide care to Veterans enrolled in more than one of the NDTH programs.

Provides and exhibits knowledge in assessment and monitoring, health restoration, wellness promotion, illness prevention, and coping facilitation. Advocates for holistic care through patient and caregiver education and provider interaction; implements an education plan to meet the patient care needs.

Develops and implements information systems to track service activities including visits, referrals, inpatient days, patient demographics, equipment utilization, and patient satisfaction.

Develops, implements and evaluates clinical guidelines and protocols to establish appropriate utilization of services to meet the needs of Veterans while supporting the VA mission.

The Nurse IV Chief Nurse (CN) functions as an advisor, administrator, educator, consultant, and mentor who possesses a wide range of experience and leadership ability.

The CN provides senior leadership and oversight for daily clinical and administrative operations within nursing as directed by the Associate Director for Patient Care Services (ADPCS.) The CN supports the integration and collaboration of nursing with other professional disciplines and functional areas in the mutual achievement of patient-centered and organizational goals.

They champion a High Reliability Organization (HRO) with a culture of safety founded on a systems approach to developing evidence-based health care solutions based on prevention, not punishment, with collective mindfulness.

The CN collaborates with interdisciplinary team members, including other program and service leaders at the facility and network. They work closely to establish and maintain effective relationships with all levels of Veteran Affairs (VA) staff nationwide.

The CN relates effectively with customers, families, and the community as well as program and service leaders at the local and network levels. They assist the ADPCS with healthcare operations and the functions and activities expected of them.

The CN contributes ideas and recommendations for the establishment of standards of care, policies, and objectives for the enhancement of nursing. Work Schedule: Full-time Monday-Friday 0730-1600 Compressed/Flexible: Not Available Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

The Outpatient Behavioral Health (BH) Registered Nurse (RN) executes position responsibilities to improve Veteran and organizational outcomes.

The psychiatric BH RN executes their position duties by providing patient-centered, recovery-oriented principles, telemental health, community-based care, and self-awareness when caring for Veterans living with BH conditions.

The BH RN actively engages in interdisciplinary team huddles and meetings, uses therapeutic communication techniques, de-escalation practices, recovery-oriented language, and educates Veterans, their families, and significant others on illnesses, medications, and treatment plans.

The BH RN assists and/or directs safety concern resolution and collaborates with program leadership to help improve Veteran and program outcomes, liaising with Inpatient BH Units, develops content as well as facilitates nurse-led psychoeducational groups, and directs teams response to psychiatric and medical emergencies.

The BH RN documents assessments, risk screens, measurement-based care tools, clinical reminders, and Veteran care plans following facility policy, maintaining professional boundaries and acting in the Veteran's best interest.

The registered nurse (RN) assigned to the outpatient Behavioral Health team collaborates with interdisciplinary treatment teams in the delivery and coordination of comprehensive care to Veterans receiving outpatient behavioral health services.

The RN may work in, be assigned to, or provide cross-coverage for any Behavioral Health Service (BHS) program, Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), or facility under the El Paso VA Health Care System based on patient care needs and operational requirements.

Assignments may include, but are not limited to, the Behavioral Health Access Team (BHAT), Primary Care Mental Health Integration (PCMHI), Behavioral Health Interdisciplinary Program (BHIP), Somatic Treatments (i.e Esketamine, etc.), Hospital Liaison, Intensive Community Mental Health Recovery (ICMHR), Housing and Urban Development-VA Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH).

The RN must maintain a current, valid, and unrestricted driver's license and possess the ability to safely operate a Government Services Administration (GSA) vehicle.

Driving responsibilities may include travel between CBOCs & Main VA Facility within the El Paso VA Health Care System, community-based and home visits, outreach activities, and minimal transportation of Veterans when necessary and consistent with VA policy and operational requirements.

This requirement supports the RN's responsibility to provide coverage and services across BHS programs, community settings, CBOCs, and other facilities that fall under the El Paso VA Health Care System.

Behavioral Health Services (BHS) provides a comprehensive range of services, including walk-in/same-day access, crisis assessment and management, group programming, evidence-based treatments, tele-mental health services, medication management, case management/Mental Health Treatment Coordinator (MHTC) services, counseling for couples and families, psychological assessment, outreach, and other behavioral health services.

The responsibilities of the Behavioral Health Registered Nurse (BH RN) include, but are not limited to, conducting risk assessments, triage, and clinical nursing services for Veterans seeking or receiving behavioral health care.

The BH RN addresses Secure Messaging (SM), Message Managers (MM), and other Veteran care requests within established facility policy and standards for timeliness, responding directly within the RN's scope of practice and appropriately routing, reassigning, or escalating requests to the appropriate team, provider, or service when indicated.

The RN reviews diagnostic and laboratory results, discusses abnormal findings with the referring or responsible provider, and communicates normal results to Veterans and/or caregivers, as appropriate. Other duties as assigned.

Duties are but not limited to: The ANM demonstrates leadership, experience, and creative approaches in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others.

The ANM, in collaboration with the Education Department, develops, coordinates, and provides ongoing education to nursing personnel for knowledge and skills enhancement while ensuring clinical competence.

The ANM may cover in the absence of the Nurse Manager and represents the Nurse Executive during non-administrative hours .The ANM RN is a professional RN qualified by education and experience to provide professional leadership in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others.

Provides professional psychiatric and/or medical nursing care to acute and chronically ill Veterans. The ANM is accountable for adhering to established policies and standards of care and practice.

The ANM is responsible for assisting the NM in supervision and administration of nursing care delivery, managing nursing personnel, and coordinating all related activities. The ANM demonstrates leadership in developing and implementing programs to improve the delivery of patient care. Will maintain clinical proficiency in area of oversight.

The ANM will evaluate procedural, pharmacological, and other therapeutic treatment regimen, monitoring to ensure compliance with all medical center policies and procedures.

Will successfully transition new hires into the position by promptly communicating performance elements and standards within applicable timeframes, providing ongoing feedback and coaching, and making appropriate use of the probationary period to assess the employee's ability to perform.

Preferred Experience: - Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) preferred; advanced nursing or leadership education is highly desirable. - Minimum of 2 or 3 years of recent nursing experience in an acute inpatient psychiatric/mental health setting preferred. - Previous charge nurse, team lead, supervisory, or nursing leadership experience preferred. - Experience caring for patients with acute psychiatric conditions, behavioral emergencies, suicide/self-harm risk, aggression, and complex behavioral needs. - Demonstrated experience with de-escalation, crisis intervention, restraint/seclusion reduction, and maintaining a safe therapeutic environment. - Knowledge of levels of observation, environmental and ligature-risk safety, contraband/hazardous-item management, and inpatient psychiatric safety practices. - Experience with staff supervision, scheduling, performance management, coaching, education, and competency development. - Experience supporting quality improvement, regulatory compliance, patient safety, and survey readiness. - Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with psychiatry, social work, psychology, nursing, VA Police, and other interdisciplinary team members. - Strong communication, conflict-resolution, clinical judgment, and leadership skills in a high-acuity environment.

VALLHCS is an interdisciplinary facility serving medical, surgical, behavioral health, inpatient, outpatients, and residential treatment. This position requires visual acuity, keen hearing, clear distinctive speech, and manual dexterity.

This position requires potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, stooping, sitting, bending, pulling, and pushing. Transferring patients and objects may be required.

The incumbent may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and may be required to don protective clothing in isolation situations or operative/invasive procedures. The incumbent will be exposed to patients who are combative secondary to delirium, dementia, or psychiatric disorders.

The incumbent must be a mature, flexible, sensible individual capable of working effectively in stressful situations, able to shift priorities based on Veteran needs.

Duties include, but are not limited to: Manages the administration and evaluation of nursing care, program implementation, personnel management, and overall operations for the Dialysis Unit, home dialysis program, and acute dialysis in the ICU units.

Manages delivery of quality patient care, including appropriate documentation, employee clinical/performance competency, and continuous National and VAPAHCS performance-improvement measures consistent with the VAPAHCS mission. Oversees and monitors employee adherence to VHA Privacy/HIPAA and Information Security rules and regulations.

Directly coordinates staffing, physical facilities, supplies, and equipment for nursing services provided to patients 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Leads retention and recruitment of highly skilled nursing staff; monitors workflow, technical, and equipment needs; and ensures the workforce can adapt to a rapidly changing environment.

Ensures employees complete mandatory annual, facility, and nursing training and reviews within required time frames. Ensures annual appraisals/proficiencies are completed, communicated to employees, and submitted timely.

Maintains familiarity with established policies and procedures; administers the unit in accordance with The Joint Commission (TJC) and VHA policy; and ensures staff compliance with VAPAHCS and unit-based policies and procedures.

Applies and completes reports related to policy and procedures, including staffing reconciliation, payroll exceptions, risk management, patient incidents, personnel accidents, EEO, and sexual-harassment allegations.

Participates in designing, implementing, monitoring, and revising systems that promote cost-effective resource use, effective staffing, and enhanced patient care using System Redesign principles.

Provides leadership and collaborates with the interdisciplinary team to improve and sustain service quality and effectiveness; applies professional practice and TJC standards to program development, analysis, and management; and promotes evidence-based practice for optimal patient outcomes.

Collaborates with the Nursing Perioperative Management Team to identify and promote staff development, strengthen staff competencies, and advance System Redesign initiatives; works with the Chief Nurse of Nursing Perioperative on program development, quality care, performance measures, and resource planning.

Maintains an integrated delivery system through expansion of clinical practices. Maintains operational efficiencies through emphasis on safe practices and National Safety. Actively implements Lean principles, supports quality-improvement projects, and promotes a culture of continuous quality improvement.

Supports excellence in research, training, and education through ongoing competency. Performs other duties as assigned.

Develops/reviews nursing functional statements, position descriptions, competencies, performance appraisals, and performance plans.

Utilizes organization, critical thinking, leadership and problem-solving skills to address/identify/resolve nursing administrative and clinical issues.

Ensures administrative and clinical applications reflect VA standards of patient education, treatment interventions, outcome re-evaluations, and adherence to Nursing Service and VA Healthcare policies, including all new VA directives.

Gathers data from personal observation to assist in ongoing improvement/customization of training for Nursing Senior Leadership and staff. Demonstrates expert knowledge and ability to apply principles of evidence-based practice, monitors and reports effectiveness of change outcomes to Nursing Senior Leadership.

The primary function of the CCICM RN is provide coordination and direct clinical evidence-based services including, assessments and interventions; program development; Veteran, family, caregiver and staff education on Care Coordination and Integrated Case Management (CCICM); resource development; community outreach; continuous quality improvement activities, and evaluation/consultation.

Duties include, but are not limited to: Serves as a CCICM subject matter expert. Participates in the development of policies, procedures, and practice guidelines for the program and participates in facility, VISN, and national program development as related to CCICM.

Ensures compliance with VHA Directive 1110.04, Integrated Case Management Standards of Practice. Provides guidance and support in the implementation and maintenance of the program through education, training, mentorship, and coaching. Participates in the development of, and implements policies and procedures specific to the Aleda E.

Lutz VA Medical Center and ensures compliance with local facility, VISN, Patient Experience Initiatives, VA Central Office (VACO) directives and handbooks, as well as Joint Commission, and other accrediting bodies and regulatory standards as needed.

Ensures full collaboration with social work counterpart, for all planning, development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of the CCICM operations. Manages, monitors, evaluates and reports on all CCICM related data to fully capture the day-to-day functioning and practice impacts on the facility and Veteran care.

Plans, organizes, and directs CCICM operations, in conjunction with the CCICM Executive Sponsor, social work counterpart(s) and the ADPCS. Identifies Veteran cohorts across the Aleda E. Lutz VA Medical Center with the highest opportunity and highest need.

Including development and implementation of a monitoring process for ongoing screening and identified cohort(s). Identifies and tracks potential areas where care coordination is taking place to include but not limited to primary care, surgical care, mental health, community care, specialty clinics, geriatrics, chronic disease, and homeless programs.

Ensures integration with the facility level care coordination and case management teams to include but not limited to Nurses and Social Workers, care coordinators, care managers, and case managers of, both inpatient and outpatient for seamless continuity of care.

Develops, implements and tracks facility wide CCICM education plan to key stakeholders to include Service Chiefs, supervisors/managers, frontline staff, and Veterans with plan for ongoing sustainment. Develops, implement, and monitor processes for ongoing screening and identified cohort. ?

Actively participates in the treatment planning process with other disciplines, including involvement in discharge planning with other disciplines and will be responsible for ensuring that discharge plans are executed in a manner that are timely and appropriate.

Actively participates in unit quality improvement processes and initiatives, as well as Veteran experience/customer service programs and initiatives. Develops, maintains effective working relationships with key medical center staff and community agencies to enhance the scope and functioning of Veterans assigned.

Ability to develop needed community support and/or resources to ensure the program goals are achieved. Provides guidance, education, and direction to the Care Coordination Review Team (CCRT).

Ensuring full participation by setting expectations, clear roles, and responsibilities when assigning a Lead Coordinator to Veterans identified as needing moderate or complex care coordination services.

Provides direct patient care services to identified high utilizer/at-risk Veterans to ensure appropriate services are in place to support the CCICM framework. Preferred: Candidates in possession of and provide proof of BLS Certification will be considered best qualified.

Physical Requirements: This position requires visual acuity, keen hearing, clear distinctive speech, and manual dexterity. This position requires potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, stooping, sitting, bending, pulling, and pushing. Transferring patients and objects may be required. Mechanical inpatient lifts are provided.

The incumbent may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and may be required to don protective clothing in isolation situations, operative/invasive procedures, or home settings. The incumbent may occasionally be exposed to patients who are combative secondary to delirium, dementia, or psychiatric disorders.

The incumbent must be a mature, flexible, sensible individual capable of working effectively in stressful situations, able to shift priorities based on patient needs. Must complete annual Employee Health requirements, such as annual TB screening or testing, as a condition of employment.

The incumbent who provides care in home settings or other off-site locations may be required to drive and/or ride in GSA-vehicles.

The Nurse Manager assumes appropriate responsibility regarding administrative and clinical issues, such as staffing coverage, granting leave, and patient and/or staff issues.

The Registered Nurse (RN) Community Living Center (CLC) provides evidence-based care to residents while supervising licensed vocational nurses and nursing assistants. The role supports nursing education, staff orientation, competency development, and quality-improvement initiatives.

The RN demonstrates leadership in promoting holistic, collaborative care and contributes to interdisciplinary teamwork to strengthen outcomes within the CLC. Responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing and/or supervising direct patient care.

Assess, plan, implement, and evaluate care based on age specific components. Assume responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care. Administer medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines.

Influence care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team. Execute position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex client care.

As the Kerrville Community Living Center (CLC) Registered Nurse (RN) you are responsible and accountable for individual nursing practice and determine the appropriate delegation of tasks consistent with the nurse's obligation to provide optimal care.

The focus is on individual growth and development in practice with increased levels of self-direction. Ability to formulate a plan of care based on nursing assessments. Seek guidance in how to improve care provided to residents and families. You will bring principles and theory with limited application of critical thinking skills.

Seek documentation guidance from the Minimum Data Set (MDS) Coordinator to ensure accuracy of the Resource Utilization Group (RUG) score.

Major duties include, but are not limited to: Analyzes issues, trends, and supporting data to determine the needs of individuals and the organization. Collects and validates data to identify professional practice gaps; determines specific knowledge, skill or practice deficits or opportunities.

Identifies desired outcomes and develops plans to outline strategies and resources. Coordinates educational activities and initiatives, employing AHA, REdI, and simulation best practices to facilitate positive, evidence-based learning environments. Evaluates progress toward attainment of desired training program outcomes.

Responsible for oversight and implementation of the ALS Program, including all course delivery (ACLS, BLS, PALS, etc.), implementation and maintenance of (AHA Resuscitation Quality Improvement, Heartcode course training delivery), REdI compliance, continuous quality improvement of emergency response patient care training delivery, tracking of staff training, managing training deficiencies, and timely reporting of program data.

Ensures all ALS training incorporates simulation (mannequin and scenario based activities), team-based code response, and standardized AHA and REdI program administration protocols.

Collaborates with the Simulation Program to integrate full-scale simulation, in-situ mock codes, and performance debriefs, ensuring transfer of learning to clinical practice. Keeps current with AHA guidelines, integrating latest best practices, cognitive aids, and emergency response algorithms in training and assessment.

Leads and participates in code incident reviews and resuscitation committee to evaluate the emergency response process, identifying and implementing opportunities for practice improvement using best practices and simulation data. Develop and oversee action plans for nursing and other clinical staff to provide ALS consultation to code team response.

Supports resuscitation committee oversight review and updates of MVHCS Medical Emergency Response standard operating procedure (SOP). Compliance oversight and maintenance of weekly safety inspections/ documentation records for Automated External Defibrillators (AED).

Responds to code events in clinical areas, providing expert ALS consultation to code teams and supporting RN duties as needed. Mentors code team members in real time and during debriefings, modeling best practice and safe resuscitation behaviors.

Rejoignez OSAD Helvetia et donnez du sens à votre métier : ensemble, faisons de chaque jour une différence pour ceux qui comptent.
OSAD Helvetia est un réseau de soins ambulatoires en pleine croissance, actif sur l’ensemble du Valais romand et du canton de Vaud. Nous proposons une offre complète de soins en cabinet, de soins à domicile, de centres de prélèvement, de transport médical ainsi que des prestations d’aide pratique, de veilles et de présences à domicile.
Autorisée par les autorités sanitaires compétentes, notre organisation place la qualité des soins, la proximité et l’accompagnement personnalisé au cœur de sa mission. Engagée durant la pandémie de COVID-19 avec la mise en place d’un centre de dépistage, OSAD Helvetia poursuit aujourd’hui son développement afin de répondre aux besoins croissants de la population.
Afin de renforcer notre équipe de liaison, nous recherchons un·e :
Infirmier·ère polyvalent·e (60 à 80 %)

En tant qu’infirmier·ère polyvalent·e, vous assurez une prise en charge globale et de qualité des patients, en collaboration étroite avec les responsables et le service de coordination, les référents des soins, les médecins, les familles et les différents partenaires du réseau de santé.
Votre activité combine soins infirmiers, coordination, prélèvements biologiques, suivi des patients et tâches médico-administratives, dans une approche centrée sur les besoins de chaque patient.
Vos principales responsabilités
1. Soins et prise en charge des patients
Dispenser des soins infirmiers ambulatoires et à domicile, adaptés à l’état de santé et à la complexité des situations.
Assurer le suivi global des patients et l’actualisation des dossiers, plans de traitement et plans de soins.
Veiller à la bonne application des prescriptions médicales.
Réagir de manière appropriée à l’évolution de l’état de santé des patients.
Garantir la continuité, la sécurité et la qualité de la prise en charge.
2. Prélèvements biologiques et soins techniques
Réaliser les prélèvements biologiques (sang, urines et autres échantillons) selon les prescriptions médicales.
Préparer le patient et le matériel nécessaire aux prélèvements.
Respecter strictement les règles d’hygiène, d’asepsie et de sécurité.
Assurer l’identification, l’étiquetage, la traçabilité et l’acheminement des prélèvements vers les laboratoires.
Garantir le double contrôle lors de toute modification de traitement, notamment pour les traitements IV.
3. Coordination et liaison
Coordonner la prise en charge avec les médecins traitants, les patients, les familles et les différents professionnels de santé.
Assurer la liaison avec les établissements de soins et les partenaires externes.
Préparer et coordonner les admissions, consultations, hospitalisations et retours à domicile.
Assurer une transmission complète et fluide des informations entre les différents intervenants.
Participer au suivi des prescriptions OPAS et aux échanges avec les assureurs.
Assurer un suivi régulier avec les médecins et partenaires impliqués dans la prise en charge.
4. Planification et organisation
Organiser et planifier les prestations, rendez-vous et interventions.
Gérer les priorités en fonction des besoins des patients et des directives institutionnelles.
Veiller au respect des délais de prise en charge et de réponse aux demandes.
Participer à l’organisation et à la répartition des activités au sein de l’équipe.
Contribuer à l’utilisation efficiente et optimale des ressources.
5. Gestion des dossiers et tâches médico-administratives
Garantir la tenue à jour des dossiers patients et la traçabilité des informations.
Documenter les soins, transmissions et actions de coordination.
Préparer et transmettre les dossiers médicaux avec l’ensemble des documents requis.
Assurer les communications par téléphone, e-mail, courrier et outils de communication internes.
Participer à l’accueil des patients et à l’orientation des demandes.
Effectuer les tâches administratives nécessaires au bon déroulement de la prise en charge.
6. Qualité, sécurité et développement des pratiques professionnelles
Garantir le respect des normes d’hygiène, d’asepsie et de sécurité.
Participer à la prévention des infections et à la sécurité des patients.
Superviser la qualité des transmissions et des prestations de soins.
Contribuer à l’amélioration continue de la qualité des soins.
Participer au développement et à l’harmonisation des pratiques professionnelles.
Contribuer au projet de service en collaboration avec la responsable et la coordinatrice des soins.
Participer au partage des connaissances, à l’accompagnement et à l’évaluation des compétences des membres de l’équipe.
Soutenir la responsable des soins et la coordinatrice dans leurs missions.
7. Logistique et gestion des ressources
Participer à la gestion des stocks de médicaments, dispositifs médicaux et consommables.
Assurer le suivi des conditions de conservation des médicaments et du matériel.
Effectuer les contrôles de température du réfrigérateur et des locaux selon les procédures en vigueur.
Veiller à la disponibilité du matériel nécessaire à l’activité.
Participer à une utilisation efficiente et responsable des ressources de l’organisation.
Votre profil
Diplôme d’infirmier·ère HES ou titre jugé équivalent et reconnu en Suisse.
Expérience professionnelle dans les soins ambulatoires, à domicile ou dans un environnement similaire.
Maîtrise des soins infirmiers et des techniques de prélèvements biologiques.
Sens aigu des responsabilités et de la sécurité des patients.
Excellentes capacités d’organisation, de coordination et de priorisation.
Autonomie, rigueur et capacité à gérer des situations variées.
Aisance relationnelle et excellente communication avec les patients, familles et professionnels de santé.
Esprit d’équipe, flexibilité et capacité d’adaptation.
Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques usuels.
Permis de conduire et véhicule personnel, un atout pour les activités à domicile.
Nous vous offrons
Un poste polyvalent, varié et responsabilisant au sein d’une organisation en plein développement.
Une activité combinant soins, coordination, prélèvements et accompagnement des patients.
Un environnement de travail dynamique, humain et collaboratif.
La possibilité de développer vos compétences et de participer activement à l’évolution des pratiques professionnelles.
Une collaboration étroite avec une équipe pluridisciplinaire et les différents partenaires du réseau de soins.
Un cadre de travail valorisant l’autonomie, la responsabilité et l’esprit d’équipe.
La possibilité de contribuer directement au développement d’une organisation engagée dans la qualité et la proximité des soins.

The Assistant Nurse Manager (ANM) supports the Nurse Manager (NM) with supervisory duties and responsibility and accountability for the 24/7 operations of their designated units. They provide coverage for other ANMs as needed.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards The Nurse Manager (NM) is the designated first-line supervisory authority and is responsible and accountable for the operation of their assigned units and provides coverage for other NMs as needed.

Responsible and accountable for the direction and supervision of specific orientation, training, development of staff, and evaluation of individual staff performance. Functions as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing leadership to the team.

Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team to remove barriers and implement new evidence-based cutting-edge programs/processes. The NM engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth.

Adheres to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. Equips staff with tools for competent care and promotes an environment of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes.

Promotes alliances across the care continuum. building trust through active listening, engagement, and emotional intelligence. The NM contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable, and equitable patient care.

Ensures compliance with accreditation and regulatory standards. Aligns nursing and clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. Promotes a workplace positively to achieve the organization's vision and mission.

The NM maintains knowledge and ensures compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards, directives, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOP). Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement. Supports colleagues and other nurses through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care.

Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes.

Evaluates outcomes of evidence-based decisions and practice changes for individuals, groups, and populations. Responsible for the documented outcomes at the program or service level.

Program or service level outcomes must be broad and complex and can be demonstrated at any organizational level within a facility Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: Full Time, 7:00am-3:30pm Compressed/Flexible: Available Telework: Yes as determined by agency Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Physical Requirements: All applicants must be physically able to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position. A pre placement examination shall be completed prior to appointment.

Major Duties include, but are not limited to: Provide direct nursing care and case management for Veterans with chronic and complex pain conditions within the primary care setting.

Collaborate with physicians, nurse practitioners, pharmacists, psychologists, and other interdisciplinary team members to develop and implement individualized pain management care plans. Conduct comprehensive pain assessments and monitor treatment efficacy and side effects.

Support safe opioid prescribing practices, including monitoring compliance with Opioid Safety Initiative (OSI) guidelines, informed consent processes, and Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) checks.

Educate Veterans and caregivers on pain management options, including non-pharmacological modalities (e.g., Whole Health, mindfulness, physical therapy referrals, acupuncture) and safe medication use.

Coordinate referrals to specialty pain clinics, behavioral health, physical medicine and rehabilitation, and complementary/integrative health services. Monitor high-risk patients for signs of substance use disorder, diversion, or adverse outcomes, and escalate concerns per protocol.

Document care thoroughly and accurately in the electronic health record (CPRS/Cerner) in compliance with VA and Joint Commission standards. Participate in quality improvement initiatives related to pain management outcomes and opioid safety metrics. Provide telephone triage and telehealth support for pain-related patient concerns.

Maintain current knowledge of VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guidelines for Opioid Therapy and Chronic Pain Management VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 8:00-4:30 pm Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

The Diabetes Educator is responsible for providing expert, evidence-based diabetes education to staff and patients. Provides educational instruction and training for diabetic patients throughout the medical facility. The Diabetes Educator understands instructional design, implementation, and application related to education and training.

Demonstrates knowledge and application of professional standards related to patient diabetes care. Performs learning needs assessments, develops educational trainings for patients and staff within organization. Develops entry level coaching and mentoring skills.

Systematically evaluates current practice, formulate appropriate diabetic outcomes for groups of patients and/or organizational processes within area of expertise.

Collaborates with other Clinical Nurse Educators and interprofessional healthcare teams in the ongoing clinical education activities including in-services, training, competency assessment, and evaluations of both current and new staff nursing skills. Acts as a consultant in patient diabetes care principles and performance measures.

Reviews current nursing literature for new diabetic trends and changes based on evidence-based research with the ability to propose practice and documentation revisions based on evaluation of outcomes. Utilizes best practices and benchmarking to establish realistic goals for patient diabetes care initiatives.

Collaborates with leadership and unit managers to identify diabetics educational training needs for staff, while supporting activities that foster competence, critical thinking skills, and decision making. Provides consultation and collaboration through the participation within organizational committees.

Ability to analyze, interpret, and evaluate data to determine outcomes and changes related to diabetes educational programs. Responsible for the documented outcomes at the program or service level.

Lab phlebotomy, point-of-care testing, and specimen labeling. The Outpatient Mental Health RN assumes the following major duties and responsibilities: 1) Is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing and/or supervising patient care. 2) Utilizes designated templates for CPRS for assigned department, and completes nursing notes in alignment with ANA Guidelines, Nursing Policy, and Nurse Competency training. 3) Serves as a liaison for warm handoffs, as needed for psychiatric concerns and initiates referrals between mental health clinics for urgent mental health needs including potential evaluation for acute Inpatient Mental health care. 4) Completes Clinical Reminders when due, and actively collaborates with treating/covering provider on required follow-up. 5) Manages secure messages for designated Providers. 6) Follows continuum of care agreements within Mental Health service and across services. 7) If indicated facilitates Measurement-Based Care (MBC) in person, by telephone and discusses finding in the development of the treatment plan with the patient and treatment team. 8) Completes a Suicide risk assessment which each mental health encounter when the patient has not already been evaluated by another clinician in the same day.

Applies additional interventions in alignment with policy, and actively communicates with their team to mitigate risk and provide needed follow-up. 9) Completes a Columbia Suicide Severity Risk Screening (CSSRS) when due or indicated & applies additional interventions in alignment with VHA Policy. 10) Completes a Suicide Behavior Overdose Reports [SBOR] when the patient reports a behavior that is not already documented and that could increase the risk for suicide such as but not limited to attempted suicide or preparatory behaviors (hoarding medication or purchasing a lethal weapon with the intent to harm self).

Communicates risk with Provider and Suicide Prevention Counselor (SPC). 11) Completes a Suicide Safety Plan in alignment with policy and in the development of the treatment plan. 12) Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient transition through the continuum of care, patient and family education, patient self management after discharge, and supporting factors that impact customer satisfaction. 13) Considers all characteristics of the individual, including age and life stages, state of health, race and culture, values, and previous experiences. 14) Demonstrates effective interpersonal skills and therapeutic interventions with patients. 15) Administers medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines. 16) Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team. 17) Core elements of performance include knowledge and active participation in unit/program level quality improvement processes and initiatives as well as customer service programs. 18) Conducts chart audits and takes remedial actions as designated by the Assistant Nurse Manager, Nurse Manger, Section Chief, or Associate Nurse Executive for Mental Health. 19) Completes Safe Patient Handling and Mobility training on hire and as designated by Assistant Nurse Manager, Nurse Manager, and Associate Nurse Executive of Mental Health. 20) Maintains appropriate level of PMDB per Assistant Nurse Manager, Nurse Manager and Associate Nurse Executive of Mental Health. 21) Other duties as designed by the IMPACT Unit per Assistant Nurse Manager, Nurse Manager, Associate Nurse Executive of Mental Health, Section Chief.
